How to get your Instagram QR code in the app

Instagram has a built-in QR code for every account. It is quick to grab and fine for sharing from your phone screen.

  1. Open the Instagram app and go to your profile.
  2. Tap the menu (three lines) in the top-right corner.
  3. Tap QR code. On some older Android versions this option is labeled Nametag, so update the app if you cannot find it.
  4. Change the look if you like (color, emoji or selfie background), then tap Share or take a screenshot to save it.

Menu names change as Instagram updates the app, so treat these steps as a guide rather than a guarantee.

Why use a custom Instagram QR code?

The in-app code is designed for showing on a screen. If you are printing flyers, stickers, packaging or a shop window sign, a screenshot is a weak starting point: low resolution, fixed styling, and no way to match your brand.

A custom code built from your profile link gives you clean PNG and vector SVG files that stay sharp at any size, colors and a logo that match your brand, and a call-to-action frame such as "Follow us on Instagram." It is a static code, so it does not expire and needs no account.

How to make an Instagram QR code

You only need your profile link.

  1. Copy your profile URL. It looks like instagram.com/yourusername. Just type your username after the domain if you know it.
  2. Paste it into the field above. The code appears as you type.
  3. Choose colors and a style. Dark code on a light background scans best.
  4. Optional: add a center logo or turn on the frame and write a short prompt.
  5. Download the PNG for social posts and screens, or the SVG for print.
  6. Scan the finished code with your phone to check that it opens the right profile.

If you later change your Instagram username, a code built from the old link will stop working. Choose a username you plan to keep before printing anything in bulk.

Where to Use It

Where an Instagram QR code works best

Storefront & packaging

A code on the window, counter, bags or product boxes turns walk-in customers into followers.

Flyers & posters

Give event and promo material a way to continue online without a long handle to type.

Add it next to your contact details so people can check your portfolio right away.

Ask happy customers to tag you or follow for specials while the visit is fresh.

Events & markets

Put a large code on a banner or table sign at pop-ups, fairs and trade shows.

Videos & slides

Show the code on a slide or video end card for viewers who want your account.

Tips for an Instagram QR code that gets scanned

A few habits make the difference between a code people scan and one they ignore.

  • Give a reason to scan: "Follow for weekly specials" beats a bare code.
  • Make sure the account is ready: a public profile with a clear bio and recent posts converts scanners better.
  • Size and contrast: keep printed codes at least about 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide, dark on light.
  • Keep any logo small: error correction rises automatically when you add one, but a big logo still hurts scanning.
  • Test on two phones (iPhone and Android) before printing a batch.
